public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Hgen is a seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Colin Ho and Molly Yang that has raised $7M to date. The broader climate and energy sector includes one public comparable (Linza: LNZA) and eight private peers spanning battery materials, hydrogen, and critical minerals extraction, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method: stage-progression analysis. Using the $7M total raised as a proxy for implied seed-stage valuation and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage step-ups yields an implied valuation of $18M. This method directly reflects capital deployment and represents the most defensible approach given data constraints.

The peer-median approach is not applicable. While eight same-sector companies exist, none satisfy narrow filtering criteria (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier), falling short of the three-datapoint minimum for meaningful triangulation. Using a broader all-sector median would introduce excessive noise and is therefore excluded.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $15M (low) to $20M (high), with a median of $18M. Key uncertainties include the absence of directly comparable seed-stage benchmarks in climate tech, limiting calibration precision, and the nascent nature of Hgen's market positioning relative to later-stage peers.
